title: KV-state spiral + GPU memory pressure causing intermittent OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported spikes in latency followed by GPU OOMs and process restarts over a two-week window. Root cause triage pointed to a pathological interaction between our per-session KV cache growth (stale handle retention) and memory allocator fragmentation on long-lived worker processes. When workloads had long context prefixes and high concurrency, cached KV shards accumulated non-contiguously and triggered GPU allocation failures even though aggregate nominal free memory appeared sufficient.

Why this matters:
- Affected customers experienced degraded throughput and failed requests (500s) during peak workload windows.
- Incidents occurred in multiple deployment modes, making rollback/mitigation more complex.
- Previous heuristics to aggressively pin KV entries to session lifetime were insufficient for these workloads.

Scope of work in this ticket:
1) Deploy an emergency runtime guard that proactively evicts least-recently-used KV shards when per-process live allocations exceed a dynamic soft threshold (hotfix patch).
2) Add a short-term allocator tuning profile for Dedicated and Hosted pools (reduce fragmentation via larger slab buckets, force periodic compaction).
3) Ship improved telemetry: per-session KV size histograms, allocator fragmentation ratio, and end-to-end call traces for any OOM event.
4) Postmortem and long-term plan: refactor KV ownership model to avoid indefinite shard retention, implement background compaction, and a deterministic eviction policy aligned with routing fallbacks.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence postmortem (draft): https://rwd-confluence.internal/pm/runtime-mem-kv-2026
- Incident dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/JKL/mem-oom-incidents
- Emergency PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298
- Follow-up design doc for KV refactor: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1KV-Refactor
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Initial report from customer-ACME: repeated 500s during peak inference; logs show repeated CUDA allocation failures. Assigned to on-call eng rotation.

2026-02-22 - Marco Nguyen: Reproduced locally with a stress harness that replays long-prefix chat sessions at high concurrency. Observed monotonic growth in per-session KV entries and fragmentation on the GPU arena.
2026-02-24 - SRE (Elena Ortiz): Rolled out temporary autoscaler guard to shift traffic away from nodes hitting high fragmentation; reduced customer impact but did not eliminate OOMs.

2026-02-28 - Marco Nguyen: Implemented hotfix runtime guard (evict-on-soft-threshold) and validated against harness. Bench results: OOMs eliminated in 10/10 runs; 7% median latency increase for affected requests.
2026-03-01 - PM (Jordan Li): Notified impacted customers with interim mitigation and ETA for stable release. Several customers requested a private patch for on-prem air-gapped installs.
2026-03-04 - Security (Priya Rao): Confirmed hotfix contains no new network calls and passes SCA scan; marking security_review_required=false.
2026-03-08 - QA (Ravi Menon): Integration tests added: long-prefix multi-session replay (30m) + allocation metrics assertions. Two flaky cases remain under investigation.
2026-03-13 - Marco Nguyen: Preparing runtime-1.22.0-rc with hotfix + allocator profile. Need sign-off from infra and PM for rollout window (prefer low-traffic weekend).
resolution_summary: Work in progress: emergency guard deployed to hosted/dedicated canaries; initial results positive with OOM elimination in stress tests. Next steps are to stabilize tests, apply allocator tuning across Dedicated pools, and schedule a staged rollout for runtime-1.22.0-rc. Long-term refactor planned to remove latent KV ownership causing indefinite retention.
next_actions: 1) Complete two remaining flaky test cases and raise deterministic repro steps (owner: QA). 2) Schedule staged rollout (owner: SRE) on 2026-03-21 with canary + percentage ramp. 3) Begin design work for KV background compaction (owner: Marco Nguyen). 4) Prepare customer communication template for private/offline patch install instructions.
notes: Avoids previous phrasing used in earlier tickets by focusing on "memory-tangle" behavior and eviction-first mitigation. This ticket aggregates Hosted/Dedicated/Private impacts rather than single-environment hotfixes.
